rationale: The workflow is a single Docker-based job (library-gradle) that checks out the repo, builds a toolbox image, runs a generator container, and compares/upload artifacts. It has no package-manager dependency installation step (Gradle, npm, pip, Go modules) that the P-LIT-GHA-CACHE dependency-cache evidence covers, so adding actions/cache would not target a measurable dependency-fetch cost in this workflow. There is no matrix, so P-LIT-FAIL-FAST does not apply. P-LIT-CUSTOM-TIMEOUT would require a safe timeout value derived from representative successful-duration history, but the provided CI history contains no job durations, and imposing an arbitrary timeout risks interrupting valid slow Docker build/generate runs. Path filtering (P-LIT-CHANGE-FILTER) is contraindicated because shared generators (toolbox/Dockerfile, generate-stackbrew-library.py) and unrelated repo changes can affect the generated library output. Cancel-stale/suppression patterns are CI-service concerns with simulation-based evidence and no clear safe fit for this official-images update workflow. No evidence-supported optimization fits without risking coverage or introducing unsupported changes.
